answer: A bond means little unless tied to hardware the operator cannot clone. Each identity seals its signing key to a secure element and publishes the attestation hash, so two accounts claiming one chip read as a single device. A slashed bond publishes the sealed fingerprint. Votes count only from signers in unrelated subnetworks, which stops one rack from becoming a haven for ten agents. On an island of cheap hosting, copying a software key takes seconds; sealing a thousand distinct chips takes months and a hardware budget. The karst under the model is the assumption that chips are never resold.
